The *Building reproducible data capsules* vignette shows how a capsule pins data and
describes it in a manifest. This one covers the three ways of putting a signature on that
work so a reader can check it: an **attestation** of a manifest, a **bundle** of a whole
capsule directory, and a **chain** that makes a sequence of manifests tamper-evident.

## Attesting a manifest

An attestation binds a signature to a manifest *and* to what the manifest covers, with an
optional note from the person signing:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-attest}
m <- mkmnf(list(dataset = "otis", rows = 1200L), env = FALSE)
key <- fipskg("ML-DSA-65")
att <- cpsatst(m, key, note = "counts as published")

res <- cpschkatst(att, m)
res$ok
res$checks
```

A verifier needs the attestation and the manifest, nothing else. Any change to the manifest
breaks it, and so does presenting a different key:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-attest-break}
m2 <- m
m2$meta$rows <- 1201L
cpschkatst(att, m2)$ok

cpschkatst(att, m, keyexp = fipskg("ML-DSA-65")$public)$ok
```

`keyexp` is how a reader pins the signer: the attestation carries the public key that
made it, but a reader who knows which key to expect should say so, or any key would do.

## Bundling a capsule

A bundle is one signed artifact covering a directory: every file is hashed (hidden files
included), the hashes and the manifest are signed, and the bundle verifies against the
directory later:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-bundle}
dir <- tempfile()
dir.create(dir)
write.csv(data.frame(x = 1:3), file.path(dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
m <- mkmnf(list(dataset = "demo"), env = FALSE)
key <- fipskg("ML-DSA-44")

b <- cpsbndl(dir, m, key, note = "as published")
cpsbndlvrf(attr(b, "path"), dir, man = m)$ok
```

Touch a byte of the data and the bundle no longer holds; the result names the file:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-bundle-break}
write.csv(data.frame(x = 1:4), file.path(dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
v <- cpsbndlvrf(attr(b, "path"), dir, man = m)
v$ok
```

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-bundle-read}
cpsbndlrd(attr(b, "path"))$attestation$note
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

## A chain of manifests

A per-manifest signature proves each manifest is intact but says nothing about the
*sequence*: a run could be deleted from the middle of a series, or two swapped, and every
remaining signature would still verify. A hash chain links each entry to the one before it,
so deletion, insertion and reordering all break it:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-chain}
ch <- chnnew()
ch <- chnapp(ch, "manifest for run 1", label = "run-1")
ch <- chnapp(ch, "manifest for run 2", label = "run-2")
ch <- chnapp(ch, "manifest for run 3", label = "run-3")
chnvrf(ch)$valid
```

Editing an entry breaks the chain and names where:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-chain-edit}
edited <- ch
edited$entries[[2]]$digest <- csha256("something else")
chnvrf(edited)$valid
chnvrf(edited)$broken_at
```

Deleting one breaks it too, which a per-manifest digest would never catch:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-chain-drop}
dropped <- ch
dropped$entries[[2]] <- NULL
chnvrf(dropped)$valid
```

### Sealing the chain

The seal covers the links *and the length* together, so one signature over the seal fixes
the whole history. Truncating the chain still seals, but to a different value:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-seal}
key <- fipskg("ML-DSA-44")
sig <- cpssign(chnseal(ch), key)
cpsvrf(chnseal(ch), sig, fipspubkey(key))

truncated <- ch
truncated$entries[[3]] <- NULL
cpsvrf(chnseal(truncated), sig, fipspubkey(key))
```

A chain whose links disagree has no seal to present at all:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-seal-none}
chnseal(dropped)
```

## Which to use

* One manifest, one signer: `cpsatst()`.
* A directory of files that must travel together: `cpsbndl()`.
* A series of runs, releases or data refreshes where order and completeness matter:
  `chnapp()` after each, sign `chnseal()` at each release.

All three accept any signing key the package knows: ML-DSA and SLH-DSA (`fipskg()`)
or XMSS (`pqckg()`, with the key state carried forward). A shared secret from
`drvkey()` is for keyed digests (`chmac()`), not for attestations: an
attestation names a public key, and a shared secret has none.


## Releases of Indigenous health tables

A chain fits data a community needs to be able to trust release after release. Here each
link pins one of the Statistics Canada tables on Indigenous health bundled with the
package, so a later reader can tell whether any release was altered or dropped:

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-indigenous-chain}
ch <- chnnew()
for (nm in c("health", "mentalhealth", "wellbeing")) {
  d <- indiex(nm)
  ch <- chnapp(ch, list(table = nm, rows = nrow(d), sha256 = dgstobj(d)),
                     label = nm)
}
chnvrf(ch)$valid
```

## The table in a picture

The chain and the bundle above record this table, one indicator per release. Its estimates and
intervals, drawn here for the first indicator, are what a reader sees after verification.

```{r attestations-bundles-chains-chain-table-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
ci_plot <- function(t, lab, main) {
  o <- order(t$estimate)
  t <- t[o, ]
  y <- seq_len(nrow(t))
  op <- par(mar = c(4, 10, 3, 1))
  on.exit(par(op))
  plot(t$estimate, y, xlim = range(t$lower, t$upper, na.rm = TRUE), yaxt = "n", pch = 19,
       col = blpal()[1], xlab = "estimate and 95% interval", ylab = "", main = main)
  segments(t$lower, y, t$upper, y, col = blpal()[1])
  axis(2, y, lab[o], las = 1, cex.axis = 0.7)
}
t1 <- d[d$indicator == d$indicator[1], ]
ci_plot(t1, t1$group, t1$indicator[1])
```
